title: InferPriv: Evaluating Inferential Privacy Leakage in LLM Assistants
abstract: arXiv:2610.34640v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Large language model (LLM)-based personal agents are increasingly deployed to handle everyday tasks on users' behalf. These agents have access to private user information, while their tasks involve communicating with third parties; this raises a critical privacy concern that agents may inappropriately reveal sensitive user information to these recipients. Existing benchmarks primarily assess direct privacy leakage, where an agent explicitly states a pre-specified secret or attribute. However, they do not capture \textit{inferential leakage}, where the model leaves indirect cues in the reply that implicitly leaks sensitive attributes. We introduce \textsc{InferPriv}, a benchmark that measures whether an honest-but-curious recipient can infer a user's sensitive attributes from an LLM's reply on routine task. Evaluating five frontier models, we find that inferential leakage substantially exceeds direct leakage across models and prompts. Und

translated_title: InferPriv：评估大语言模型助手中的推理型隐私泄露
translated_abstract: 基于大语言模型（LLM）的个人智能体正日益被部署用于代表用户处理日常事务。这些智能体能够访问用户的私密信息，而其任务又涉及与第三方进行沟通，这引发了一个关键的隐私担忧：智能体可能会不恰当地向这些接收者泄露用户的敏感信息。现有基准主要评估直接隐私泄露，即智能体明确陈述某个预先指定的秘密或属性。然而，它们并未涵盖推理型泄露，即模型在回复中留下间接线索，从而隐性泄露敏感属性的情况。我们提出了 InferPriv，这是一个用于衡量“诚实但好奇”的接收者能否从大语言模型对日常任务的回复中推断出用户敏感属性的基准。通过对五个前沿模型进行评估，我们发现推理型泄露在各模型和各提示下都大幅超过直接泄露……
tldr: 本文提出InferPriv基准，首次系统评估大语言模型助手在日常任务回复中通过间接线索造成的推理型隐私泄露，发现这种泄露在多个前沿模型中显著超过直接泄露。
en_tdlr: This paper introduces InferPriv, a benchmark measuring whether an honest-but-curious recipient can infer users' sensitive attributes from LLM assistants' replies to routine tasks, finding that inferential leakage substantially exceeds direct leakage across frontier models.
